assets.description: The 2013 East Span: the self-anchored suspension span (624 m, 385 m main span) with its single 160 m tower of four pentagonal steel legs joined by shear links, one main cable looped around the west end of the twin decks in four inclined planes with suspenders splayed to the outer box edges, the two side-by-side orthotropic decks (five lanes each) joined by crossbeams, the bike and pedestrian path on the south side, the Skyway's haunched concrete girders on paired T-columns descending toward Oakland, the YBI transition ramp and the Oakland touchdown. Road-fitted bridge built on the mapped OSM carriageways.

source.provenance: Original procedural geometry authored 2026-10-01 from published spans and heights (Caltrans/MTC fact sheets, T.Y. Lin WCEE paper, CGS SMIP04 paper), the mapped OSM carriageways, their separation, the tower outline, the crossbeams between the decks, the Alexander Zuckermann Bay Bridge Trail and the YBI ramps (retrieved 2026-10-01 through the OSM API, ODbL 1.0, © OpenStreetMap contributors; way ids in bay-bridge-east-span-alignment.js), and Wikimedia Commons photographs. No third-party mesh, scan, photograph or texture is shipped; reference photographs were kept in ignored local study files only. Images consulted: Caltrans, SAS elevation and plan (CalDOT-SASElevPlan4Q2005P42.svg, public domain); Mariordo (Mario Roberto Durán Ortiz), Bay Bridge 04 2015 new eastern span (CC BY-SA 4.0); Crossing the Bay Bridge, Flickr (CC BY 2.0); Earth Science Eastern Span DSC 0670, Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0); Leonard G., SFOakBayBridgeNewEastTowe (CC0); San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge, helicopter views 1 and 3, Flickr (CC BY 2.0).

assets.notes: Sourced: SAS 624.385 m (10 + 180 + 385 + 49.385 m), tower 160 m with four steel shafts and shear links, single 0.78 m cable anchored in the deck at E2 and looped around W2, suspenders every 10 m splayed to the outer box edges, two 25 m decks with five lanes each, 4.8 m path on the south (eastbound) side, crossbeams every 30 m, Skyway 2.1 km of precast segmental girders 5.5 m deep at mid-span and 9 m at the piers on 14 pairs of piers 45-115 ft tall. Mapped (OSM): both carriageways (41.8 m apart on the SAS and Skyway, converging to 26 m where the alignment starts on YBI), the tower outline (its centroid is the origin; W2 and E2 from the published spans land 0.2 and 0.3 m from the mapped crossbeams), the deck outlines (box and path edges), the crossbeam stations, the trail and the YBI ramps. Estimated: the real deck height (about 57 m over the SAS from the Caltrans elevation, SPEC.realDeckM; 22 m at E16), Skyway pier stations (not mapped; E3 160 m past E2, nine 160 m then four 122.5 m spans), tower leg sections and taper, shear-link spacing, cable sag shape, box and girder sections, YBI transition and touchdown structures, light poles. Flat-map convention (a compromise below the real deck): constant grades with parabolic vertical curves; 15.05 % from the YBI foot to ~30 m at the SAS west end (the westbound viaduct climbs over the eastbound one toward the double-deck tunnel just west of the alignment, so the ramp is 224 m), 5.3 % over the back span to 40 m at the tower, level across the main span, down the Skyway to 22 m at E16 and 4.4 % over the touchdown onto the mapped on-grade I-80. Not modelled: the old East Span piers kept as viewpoints, the belvederes, the cable bands, the night lighting of the tower and cables. The exported GLB is authored on the real profile; Cityscape lowers deck and superstructure together (tower top 142.5 m there, 160 m in world and in the inspector). Near 73 304 triangles / 33 draws / 2.79 MB; far 22 692 / 7 / 0.84 MB. No Tesla hardware measurements.

assets.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge (West Span)
assets.location: I-80, Rincon Hill to Yerba Buena Island · San Francisco, California
assets.description: The 1936 West Span: two suspension bridges end to end (side spans 1160 ft, main spans 2310 ft) sharing the concrete central anchorage W4, four silver X-braced battered steel towers, two 26 in cables, and a 66 ft by 35 ft double-deck stiffening truss carrying I-80 westbound on top and eastbound inside, from the San Francisco anchorage and SoMa viaduct to the Yerba Buena Island tunnel. The north suspenders carry the Bay Lights at night.

source.provenance: Original procedural geometry authored 2026-10-01 from the HAER CA-32 documentation, Wikipedia, the mapped OSM roadway and support outlines, and Wikimedia Commons photographs. Mapped alignment and supports © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0). No third-party mesh, scan, photograph or texture is shipped; reference photographs were kept in ignored local study files only. Photographs consulted: Dllu, 'San Francisco Bay Bridge Western Span at night' (CC BY-SA 4.0); Dllu, 'Western Span of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge at dusk, seen from Yerba Buena Island' (CC BY-SA 4.0); Radosław Botev, 'Western span of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge' (CC BY 3.0 pl); Daderot, 'Western span of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge - DSC06513' (CC0).

Far LOD (2-5 km) draws the truss as its chords and deck slab, every fourth suspender, and keeps the towers, W4 and the cables. Near 59 825 triangles / 29 draws / 2.54 MB; far 11 396 / 8 / 0.45 MB. Planting, interior, trees and surrounding paths are not modelled; the small utility building beside the south-west facade (OSM way 1420082168) is not included. Model heights are over entrance grade.

assets.notes: The 160 m x 157 m plan comes from OpenStreetMap and the 38.1 m height from its tag; every height inside it, the three-band drum profile (lower band flaring out to a ledge, middle band, top band leaning in under the visor), the 3.5 m glass lean, the 6.5-10.5 m visor depth, the roughly 11.5 m column spacing, the panel-slot rhythm, the curtain-wall grid, the sign's letter forms and size and all colours are estimates from photographs. The mapped outline is the roof edge: bands and base are tucked 0.3-4.5 m inside it. The two mapped 'notch' edges where the glass prow meets the drum are drawn as return walls banded like the drum (ledge, shadow gaps, slots, recessed base) with a short plain transition wall at the glass end. The 2.8 m west-entrance tip in the outline is smoothed away and three glazed entrance bays are placed from OSM entrance and box-office nodes. The Seeing Spheres (Olafur Eliasson), the Thrive City pavilions, the Uber towers and the cantilevered terraces north of the front are outside the mapped arena or not modelled. The blue octagon beside the sign is a plain simplification, not the artwork. Interior and seating are not modelled; the roof's parapet, radial ribs, four skylight bands, sixteen plant units and central plant block are plausible inventions (the real layout is not published). The panel slots are single hinged quads. Night: the prow's lit floors, the lobby and the entrance bays use `glow`, the sign is self-lit. `glow` is drawn unshaded, so its day colour is a deep blue chosen to match the shaded glass.

assets.name: Conservatory of Flowers
assets.location: 100 John F Kennedy Drive, Golden Gate Park · San Francisco, California
assets.description: The 1879 Victorian wood-and-glass greenhouse, the oldest building in Golden Gate Park: an octagonal pavilion under a glazed dome, drum and lantern (about 18 m) with a gabled vestibule on its south face, two vaulted wings of arch-framed glass 73 m long overall that turn toward the lawn in cupola-crowned lobes (the shallow E-shaped plan), and the low service houses behind. Roofs are shaded glass with white arch ribs; the walls, drum and lantern are lit glazing that glows warm at night.

assets.name: Canadian Museum of History
assets.description: Douglas Cardinal's 1989 museum on the Ottawa River facing Parliament Hill, both wings: the southern public wing with the glass-fronted Grand Hall behind a colonnade of flared stone piers under a layered, wave-like cornice, verdigris copper domes (the long dome, the north rotunda, the 27 m west dome) and copper-roofed strips; and the northern curatorial wing, a cascade of four stepped, curving stone terraces under a copper roof, 4.5 to 15 m high. assets.name: Édifice Marie-Guyart
assets.location: 675 boulevard René-Lévesque Est (1037 rue De La Chevrotière), Québec
assets.description: Complexe G (Gauthier, Guité, Roy, Fiset et Deschamps; Édouard Fiset, 1967-72): Québec City's tallest building, a brutalist 132 m tower of grey-taupe precast concrete on a 42 m by 47 m plan. Glazed ground storey set back under the upper floors; on all four faces a continuous ribbon of dark glass under a row of square windows in protruding precast frames; wide, plain, braced corner shafts that stand above the roof and 1 m proud of the windows; a glazed belvedere floor (Observatoire de la Capitale); a rooftop penthouse and a 177 m mast. Beside it the low government complex: three 4-level wings with cantilevered upper storeys and five 5-level stair and plant cores round an open court.

assets.description: Harry Edward Prindle's 1915 Canadian Pacific station in Québec's Lower Town, a Château-style cousin of the Château Frontenac: red-brown brick with grey limestone trim under steep verdigris copper mansard roofs. Estimated from photographs and the outline (no other published dimension was found; about 10 %): the octagon apothem 26.5 m, eaves 19.5 m, gable apexes 29 m, the portal tower (24 m wide at the base, 10.4 m at the 36 m crown), the arch (16 m wide, 24.5 m high, set back 3.2 m), the lantern (8 m across, 58 to 64.6 m) and spire, the gallery depth and pavilion size, window and rose positions, the 8 dormers and the roof patchwork (fall-line streaks of light and dark copper; the far roof is one mid colour, the near mean). Which faces carry gables (the four diagonal ones, from the photographs) and the plain side and choir walls are read from photographs; the back of the building and the sacristy are inferred from the outline. The mapped outline draws the left gallery thinner than the right one, so the symmetric galleries and pavilions stand up to 3.8 m outside it. Not modelled: the interior, ornament and lettering, the stair railings, stone coursing on the side walls, the Petit Sanctuaire, the plaza and the visitor pavilion. Night: the stained glass and the dormer windows are self-lit (glow); the real building is floodlit. Flat-map grade y=0 is the plaza at the foot of the portal stair (the portal floor is 2.2 m above it). No Tesla hardware measurement was made. assets.name: Pont de Québec
assets.location: Route 175, the CN railway and a walkway over the St. Lawrence · Québec (Sainte-Foy)–Lévis, Québec
assets.description: The 1917 Quebec Bridge (opened 1919 after the 1907 and 1916 collapses), still the world's longest cantilever span: 548.6 m between the main piers, 987 m long. Two dark charcoal-brown steel K-trusses 26.8 m apart: 157 m anchor arms rising from tall granite anchor piers to 104 m main posts on pin shoes, 176.8 m cantilever arms and the camel-backed 195 m suspended span, the bottom chords dipping in a V to each main pier while the floor runs level at 48 m through the trusses. Route 175 (three lanes) runs inside the east truss beside the walkway, the CN track near the centre line, under portals at least 6.5 m above the road. Short deck-truss approach spans to the clifftop abutments. Road-fitted bridge built on the mapped OSM Route 175 roadway.

assets.name: Pont Dubuc
assets.location: Route 175 over the Saguenay · Chicoutimi–Chicoutimi-Nord (Saguenay), Québec
assets.description: The Route 175 crossing of the Saguenay at Chicoutimi, opened in October 1972 to replace the 1933 Pont de Sainte-Anne: a plain, functional steel girder bridge rather than an architectural one. A 458 m continuous dark-green steel box girder in seven spans carries a 22.8 m deck (four lanes either side of a median wall, a sidewalk behind a barrier on each side, railed parapets) on six pale twin-column concrete piers whose square columns rise from a battered wall, and a concrete end pier at the Chicoutimi end; inclined steel brackets reach from the box out to the fascia girders under the wide overhangs. Thirteen double-arm lamp posts stand on the median wall. Road-fitted bridge built on the two mapped OSM Route 175 carriageways.

assets.name: Pont Laviolette
assets.location: Autoroute 55 over the St. Lawrence · Trois-Rivières–Bécancour, Québec
assets.description: The 1967 A-55 crossing of the St. Lawrence, the only bridge over the river between Montréal and Québec: 2,707 m long. A continuous turquoise steel truss carries the four-lane deck through 1,383 m; over the navigation channel its top chords sweep up into a through arch (crown 106.6 m, 335 m main span: a 269 m arch hung on rope hangers between two 33 m cantilevers) whose lower chords dip through the deck in a V to the two main piers, flanked by 167 m anchor spans and three 119 m through-truss spans each side. Long plate-girder and precast approaches on twin-column piers climb from both shores over the streets beneath. Road-fitted bridge built on the two mapped OSM A-55 carriageways.

assets.name: Pont Papineau-Leblanc
assets.location: Autoroute 19 over the Rivière des Prairies · Montréal (Ahuntsic)–Laval, Québec
assets.description: The 1969 A-19 crossing of the Rivière des Prairies between Montréal (Ahuntsic) and Laval, one of the first cable-stayed bridges in North America and the first with its towers in the roadway median. A rust-brown weathering-steel box girder with an orthotropic deck carries six lanes over a 241 m main span and two 90 m side spans (421 m); two single square steel pylons (near-black chocolate, sRGB 55/42/36, against the rust-brown deck) rise 38.4 m above the deck in the median, each holding a fan of two stays a side in the central plane, on round concrete piers in the river. Road-fitted bridge built on the two mapped OSM A-19 carriageways.

West screen faces 268.1°. Estimated from the DXR west photograph and the Bjørkan east aerial: statue rows as relief bands (not the restored portraits), rose spokes, portal with a trumeau, flying-buttress rhythm on the seven aisle nibs, spire ribs, gable niche. Not modelled: interior vaults, the 2015 gable scaffold, carved canopies as individual figures, the real cruciform chapter house (a hall with an east apse instead), and the thin north and south octagon lobes (only the east chapel fits the outline). Near 36194 triangles / 7 draws / 1602220 bytes; far 8039 / 7 / 369680. Light stone is grey-green soapstone #6f746c and the copper is muted verdigris #5f9a82. Tall west-tower lancets sit above the gallery band. QA revision 2026-10-11: West-screen and tower-front pointed canopy arcades with grouped projecting figures and shelves, concentric rose surround and branching tracery, and grouped side openings. Relief is architectural approximation, not individual restored sculpture; far preserves niche rhythm with planar pointed canopies. Tower-front masonry sits 0.40 m behind its former plane so the three sculpture tiers are exposed and held by their projecting shelves. Near 36194 triangles / 7 draws / 1602220 bytes; far 8118 triangles / 7 draws / 372340 bytes. Follow-up QA 2026-10-11: Filled the blank panels beside the rose with four tall canopied bays, each carrying three statue silhouettes on shelves, and added paired niche rows to the gable. All groups survive in far; sculptural portraits remain approximations. Current exports: near 38724 triangles / 7 draws / 1719016 bytes; far 9228 triangles / 7 draws / 427820 bytes.
